answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity work deposit that is earned, not bought: an agent must stake tokens it can only recover after an epoch's ledge of grading is settled, and each new identity starts with a zero ledge balance, so minting a thousand puppet accounts gains nothing until each one independently pays the full proof-of-work cost. A relic of past epochs, the identity's settlement record, cannot be copied to a fresh key. The meadow of bonded identities therefore grows only at real marginal cost, and a wave of clones burns far more capital than the reward it could capture.
